title: Farzi Café Lands in Bellevue: The 'Prince of Indian Cuisine' Launches His Coast-to-Coast American Dream
excerpt: Zorawar Kalra's Michelin Guide-recognised modern Indian bistro opens its first US outpost in Washington state, with plans to blanket the country.
body:
Zorawar Kalra has been called the "Prince of Indian Cuisine" — a title he inherited by temperament as much as lineage. His father, the late Jiggs Kalra, was known across India as the "Czar of Indian Cuisine," a culinary polymath who shaped the country's fine-dining landscape for decades. Now the younger Kalra is doing something his father never attempted at scale: convincing America that Indian food belongs at the very centre of its restaurant universe.

Farzi Café, Kalra's flagship modern Indian bistro, has opened its first US location at The Bellevue Collection in Bellevue, Washington — a deliberate choice that puts the brand squarely in the heart of the Pacific Northwest's tech corridor, home to tens of thousands of Indian-American professionals. But Kalra has made clear this is just the beginning. "My vision is to make Indian cuisine a mainstream cuisine across the U.S.," he told *The Indian Eye* at the launch. "We plan to open restaurants in various locations throughout the country, coast to coast."

## From Delhi to Eleven Countries

The Bellevue opening represents the latest chapter in a remarkable expansion story. Kalra's Massive Restaurants group now operates more than two dozen restaurants across 11 countries, from Dubai and Doha to London and Toronto. Farzi Café London has earned recognition in the prestigious Michelin Guide — a distinction vanishingly few Indian restaurants outside the subcontinent have achieved.

The concept itself is built around what Kalra calls "molecular Indian" — traditional dishes reimagined through modern culinary techniques and theatrical presentation. The name *farzi* means "illusion" in Hindi, and the menu delivers on that promise: Dal Chawal Arancini transform comfort food into golden-fried spheres; Avocado & Raw Mango Chaat marries California's favourite fruit with Mumbai's street-food tradition; Parle-G Cheesecake turns a biscuit every Indian child grew up eating into a refined dessert.

## Why Bellevue, Why Now

The choice of Bellevue — rather than, say, Manhattan or the Bay Area — is strategic. The city sits across Lake Washington from Seattle and has become a second downtown for the region's tech industry, with Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, and Google all maintaining major offices nearby. The Indian-American population in the greater Seattle metro has surged in recent years, creating a built-in audience that understands the cuisine's nuances but craves restaurant experiences that match the ambition of what they find in Delhi, Mumbai, or London.

Kalra flew in his core team from New Delhi and London for the opening, including Executive Chef Gaurav Chawla and Engjell Shala, the group's head of beverage R&D globally. The approach signals how seriously Massive Restaurants is treating its American debut — this is not a franchise handoff but a hands-on transplant of the brand's DNA.

## A Crowded Field, But a Different Pitch

Farzi Café enters an American market that is finally warming to Indian cuisine at scale. Wonder, the $1.5-billion food-hall venture, launched its Indian concept Dabba across 100-plus storefronts this month. Dishoom and Gymkhana, London's celebrated Indian dining rooms, are exploring US openings. Semma, the Michelin-starred South Indian restaurant in New York, proved that regional Indian food could earn America's highest critical honours.

But Kalra's pitch is different from all of these. Where Dabba targets the delivery crowd with $19.95 butter chicken, and Semma leans into Tamil authenticity, Farzi Café occupies a middle ground: upscale but not austere, innovative but rooted in recognisable flavours. Achari Chicken Tacos and Karela Calamari signal a kitchen that is comfortable crossing cultural lines without losing its Indian soul.

## The Diaspora Angle

For the estimated 4.8 million Indian Americans, a coast-to-coast Farzi Café chain would represent something emotionally significant: a homegrown Indian brand competing on equal footing with the world's most powerful restaurant groups. Indian dining in America has historically been a mom-and-pop affair — beloved neighbourhood curry houses run by immigrant families. Massive Restaurants brings corporate-grade systems, global supply chains, and a Michelin pedigree to a category that has struggled to scale.

Whether that formula translates to Middle America remains to be seen. But Kalra, characteristically, is already looking past the question. "The challenges are real," he acknowledged. "Retaining top talent is a constant priority. But the appetite for Indian food in America has never been stronger."

The Bellevue restaurant is open daily. A New York City location in Tribeca at 78 Leonard Street is already serving diners, with additional cities reportedly in active planning.
